newsitem.title: CHINA: Death toll from south China floods put at 105.
newsitem.headline: Death toll from south China floods put at 105.

text.p: Flooding has wreaked havoc in southern China, killing at least 105 people and causing losses totalling one billion yuan ($120 million), officials said on Monday.

Storms triggered floods in three areas of Guangdong province last week, killing 105 people, an official with the provincial flood control headquarters said by telephone from Guangdong's capital Guangzhou.
Officials have described the floods as "occurring only once every five centuries".
About 15,160 houses collapsed and 363,000 people were left homeless, the official said.
Rivers burst their dikes flooding some 23,000 hectares (57,000 acres) of farmland and causing losses of one billion yuan, the official said.
In 1996, floods killed more than 2,000 people across China, affected about 300 million people and caused damage to property worth more than 200 billion yuan ($24.1 billion).
